handbookNote: SCOPING (confirmed 2026-08, do not re-derive): Alaska is an APPLICATION-ONLY notary state -- no exam and no mandatory training course for the base commission. Confirmed via ltgov.alaska.gov/notaries: commissioning requires only a completed application, a $2,500 official bond (AS 44.50.034), the oath/affirmation (AS 44.50.035), and a ~$40 application fee set by regulation under AS 44.50.033 -- there is no statutory testing requirement anywhere in the chapter. Product framing is therefore NOT exam prep; it is a self-study/reference practice-question set covering real state notary law (notarial duties, liability, and procedure), useful even though Alaska requires no formal test. STATUTE: AS 44.50 (Notaries Public), sections .010-.200, non-sequential numbering -- 27 operative sections located and grounded (all numeric gaps in the .010-.200 range were individually probed against a live FindLaw mirror and confirmed non-existent, since akleg.gov returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches); plus AS 09.63 (Oath, Acknowledgment, and Other Proof), a complete run of 13 sections (.010-.130), which supplies real substantive cross-referenced certificate-content rules (acknowledgment/verification/notarization form and content requirements, out-of-state and foreign notarial-act recognition under the Uniform Recognition of Acknowledgments Act at AS 09.63.050-.130) that AS 44.50 itself repeatedly incorporates by reference (e.g. AS 44.50.200(8) defines 'notarial act' by cross-referencing AS 09.63.120). CONTENT DEPTH: real and non-trivial -- full remote/electronic notarization provisions (AS 44.50.075 communication-technology/remotely-located-individual notarization with audiovisual-recording and identity-proofing requirements; AS 44.50.145 tamper-evident electronic-record technology selection; AS 44.50.185 relation to the federal E-SIGN Act); a mandatory notary journal with 10-year retention (AS 44.50.078) that is textually tied specifically to AS 44.50.075 remote acts, not to notarization generally; confidentiality protections for a notary's designated-confidential contact information (AS 44.50.071). QUIRKS WORTH REMEMBERING: (1) postmasters may perform notarial acts in Alaska WITHOUT any bond or commission, per the explicit carve-out at AS 44.50.180(d) -- a sharp contrast to the $2,500 bond otherwise required of every other notary under AS 44.50.034; (2) Alaska issues two distinct commission types under AS 44.50.010(a) -- 'notaries public without limitation' (full authority, $2,500 bond, 4-year term) versus 'limited governmental notaries public' (government employees only, official-business-only seal use, no bond requirement, term coincides with employment, application fee waived for state employees) -- and a person may hold both simultaneously per AS 44.50.010(c). SOURCE: compiled to temp/handbooks/ak/notary.txt from codes.findlaw.com/ak/ (akleg.gov itself 403'd automated fetches; FindLaw pages self-report 'current as of January 01, 2025' and were spot-checked for internal cross-reference consistency across sections). PRICING: $0.75 (75 cents) -- re-tiered 2026-08-16 against the AL/FL/GA/TX reference range (those 4 education-only tracks landed at 138-224 questions after depth expansion); Alaska's real content ceiling (106 questions) sits below that range, so it takes the middle 'solid but lighter' tier rather than the top $0.99 tier (reserved for states whose real content ceiling lands within/close to 138-224, e.g. DE/NH/ND/VA/WA/WV) or the bottom $0.50 tier (reserved for genuinely thin states like MN). QUESTION COUNT: 106 grounded questions were produced across 5 topic buckets (commissioning/qualifications/application; duties/prohibited-acts/seal/journal; remote & electronic notarization; acknowledgments/verification/certificates under AS 09.63; interstate recognition/postmasters/liability/definitions) -- this landed below the initially estimated ~100-130 ceiling's midpoint because the 'better nothing than nonsense' quality rule was followed: no filler, invented facts, or trivial rewordings were added purely to hit a higher number.
